reaction.hydrogen-combustion.title: Hydrogen combustion
reaction.hydrogen-combustion.accessibili: Two hydrogen molecules react with one oxygen molecule to form two water molecules. The reaction releases heat and requires an ignition source to start.
reaction.methane-combustion.title: Methane combustion
reaction.methane-combustion.accessibilit: One methane molecule reacts with two oxygen molecules to form one carbon dioxide molecule and two water molecules. The reaction releases heat and requires an ignition source to start.
reaction.magnesium-oxide-synthesis.title: Magnesium burns in oxygen
reaction.magnesium-oxide-synthesis.acces: Two magnesium atoms react with one oxygen molecule to form two units of magnesium oxide. The reaction releases heat and light, and requires an ignition source to start.
reaction.sodium-chloride-synthesis.title: Sodium reacts with chlorine
reaction.sodium-chloride-synthesis.acces: Two sodium atoms react with one chlorine molecule to form two units of sodium chloride, common table salt. The reaction releases heat.
reaction.ammonia-synthesis.title: Ammonia synthesis (Haber process)
reaction.ammonia-synthesis.accessibility: One nitrogen molecule reacts with three hydrogen molecules to form two ammonia molecules. Industrially this reaction is reversible and needs a catalyst, high pressure, and moderate heat.
reaction.aluminium-oxide-synthesis.title: Aluminium burns in oxygen
reaction.aluminium-oxide-synthesis.acces: Four aluminium atoms react with three oxygen molecules to form two units of aluminium oxide. The reaction releases heat and requires an ignition source to start.
reaction.calcium-carbonate-decomposition: One unit of calcium carbonate breaks down on heating into one unit of calcium oxide and one molecule of carbon dioxide gas. The reaction absorbs heat.
reaction.hydrogen-peroxide-decomposition: Two hydrogen peroxide molecules break down into two water molecules and one oxygen molecule. The reaction releases heat and is sped up by a catalyst.
reaction.potassium-chlorate-decompositio: Two units of potassium chlorate break down on heating into two units of potassium chloride and three oxygen molecules.
reaction.zinc-copper-sulfate-displacemen: Solid zinc reacts with a copper sulfate solution. Zinc takes the place of copper, forming a zinc sulfate solution and depositing solid copper.
reaction.barium-sodium-sulfate-double-di: Barium chloride reacts with sodium sulfate
Barium chloride solution reacts with sodium sulfate solution. The ions exchange partners, forming solid barium sulfate and sodium chloride in solution.
reaction.hydrochloric-acid-neutralizatio: Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide in a one-to-one ratio, forming sodium chloride and water. The reaction releases heat.
reaction.silver-chloride-precipitation.a: Silver nitrate solution reacts with sodium chloride solution. A white solid, silver chloride, forms and settles out, leaving sodium nitrate in solution.
reaction.iron-rusting.title: Iron rusting
reaction.iron-rusting.accessibility: Four iron atoms react with three oxygen molecules to form two units of iron(III) oxide, commonly known as rust. The reaction releases heat slowly at room temperature.
